Chapter 253: Chinese Universities Gather Together

What can a group of drunk men do in a private room at a business KTV?

When they woke up, they themselves didn't know what they had done.

They had blacked out.

Chen Guiliang vaguely remembered making a final phone call to Yang Shuo. As for how he got back to the hotel, his mind was a complete blank.

Right, I think I recorded something with my phone.

Chen Guiliang opened his phone and searched, only finding a video clip just over ten seconds long.

Tao Chenggang, with his raspy, off-key voice, was singing a duet of *The Boat Tracker's Love* with a girl. Shi Yuzhu and Zhou Hongwei were dancing together, wrapped in an embrace, while the girls who were supposed to be keeping them company stood to the side, clapping.

Damn it, I can hold this video over you guys for the rest of my life!

He immediately called Shi Yuzhu. "Boss Shi, time to get up."

Shi Yuzhu was groggily woken by the ringing. He fumbled for his phone with his eyes still closed, finally pressing it to his ear and saying, "Hello, who is this?"

"It's me, Chen Guiliang," said Chen Guiliang. "Hurry and get up for the Sanguosha finals."

Shi Yuzhu was still half-asleep. "What finals?"

Chen Guiliang said, "You promised me last night when we were drinking."

"I did? Let me sleep for a few more minutes." Shi Yuzhu hung up the phone.

He often made promises to people while drinking, like providing a business guarantee for someone, or lending someone a few million.

Regardless of whether he remembered it after waking up, as long as the request wasn't too outrageous, he would always make good on it afterward.

Chen Guiliang then called Zhou Hongwei. "Boss Zhou, get up. Time for the Sanguosha finals."

"Huh?" Zhou Hongwei was a little confused.

He looked at the contact name saved as "Chen Guiliang" and couldn't recall when they had exchanged numbers.

Chen Guiliang said mischievously, "I have an exciting video to show you. You'll regret it if you don't see it."

"What time do I need to be there?" Zhou Hongwei asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "The leaders' speeches are at nine. It's fine if you get there at nine-thirty."

"Alright, got it," said Zhou Hongwei.

Next, Chen Guiliang called Tao Chenggang and Chi Yufeng. The two of them were quite brisk. They got up immediately after receiving the call and even arranged to have breakfast together.

Last night, everyone had returned to hotels near the National Exhibition and Convention Center, so they weren't far from each other. They agreed to meet at the restaurant of one of the hotels.

Before long, Shi Yuzhu and Zhou Hongwei also arrived late.

Chen Guiliang took out his phone with a wicked smile and showed the video to Zhou Hongwei. "Boss Zhou, I accidentally recorded this last night."

"What is it?" Zhou Hongwei leaned in.

The video started with Tao Chenggang singing a duet with a girl, his arm around her. "Little sister, you sit at the boat's head, big brother walks on the shore..."

Zhou Hongwei laughed. "Haha, his singing is awful... Hmm?"

The camera then panned to a drunken Shi Yuzhu and Zhou Hongwei, arms wrapped around each other, swaying unsteadily as they tried to ballroom dance. Their assigned girls were clapping on the side, one of them bent over with laughter.

"Holy shit, delete it! Now!" Zhou Hongwei reached out to snatch the phone.

Chi Yufeng asked, "What's on it?"

Zhou Hongwei said to Shi Yuzhu, "He filmed a video of us dancing together. Quick, let's grab it and delete it!"

Shi Yuzhu looked baffled. "The two of us? Dancing together?"

Zhou Hongwei said, "You must have been the one to grab me first, you bastard."

"Then what are we waiting for?" Shi Yuzhu shot to his feet.

The two of them rushed over to Chen Guiliang, grabbed his wrists from both sides, and forcibly snatched the phone away.

Chen Guiliang didn't put up much of a fight, only bluffing them, "I have a backup."

"Like hell you have a backup." Zhou Hongwei started searching for the video to delete it.

Shi Yuzhu, however, was curious. "Don't be in a rush to delete it, let me see it first."

Chi Yufeng and Tao Chenggang also crowded around.

How could Zhou Hongwei let more people see it? He was about to delete it on the spot but Shi Yuzhu snatched the phone from him.

Shi Yuzhu played the video.

A few seconds later, everyone except Zhou Hongwei burst into laughter.

Including Shi Yuzhu.

Zhou Hongwei urged, "Hurry up and delete it."

But Shi Yuzhu was taking out his own phone. "I'll send it via Bluetooth."

"Damn it, you want to save it, don't you?" Zhou Hongwei quickly tried to grab it back.

Shi Yuzhu was just joking. After teasing him for a moment, he deleted the video.

Zhou Hongwei was finally relieved. He said to them, "Do any of you play live-action CS? I played it in Shenzhen last year, and they have it in Beijing now too. Drinking is actually pretty boring. Playing with guns is a man's romance!"

Shi Yuzhu asked, "Real guns?"

"Paintball guns. You've played CS, right? It's just an offline, live-action version," Zhou Hongwei explained.

Shi Yuzhu said, "That sounds interesting."

Zhou Hongwei said, "Next time you guys are in Beijing, I'll take you to play live-action CS." He then said to Chen Guiliang and Chi Yufeng, "You two are already in Beijing, we can meet up to play sometime. I'm a beast with the AK!"

"Sure," Chen Guiliang agreed at once.

What man doesn't like playing with guns?

Hearing that there was already a paintball field in Beijing, Chen Guiliang not only wanted to go himself, but he would also take his ByteDance and Youke employees there for a team-building activity at the end of the year.

Zhou Hongwei had only three hobbies: soccer, live-action CS, and collecting high-end audio equipment.

Seeing Chen Guiliang agree, he was instantly delighted to have recruited another gun-playing buddy.

Chi Yufeng said to Chen Guiliang, "My flight is this afternoon, so I can only drop by your finals for a little while in the morning."

"Just showing up is enough. Thanks for helping to draw a crowd," Chen Guiliang said. "If any of you use social networking sites, you can also register an account on Hainei. It has a follower function, so you can gather a group of your own fans. Celebrities like Andy Lau and Fan Bingbing have also joined."

Shi Yuzhu was the first to agree. "I'll go check it out."

This guy would later love to post sarcastic remarks on Weibo.

For example, his sardonic post about Dongzi: "Landed in arrogant America. My rules while in the US: 1, Don't drink; 2, Don't force women to drink; 3, Don't get to know female exchange students; 4, Don't be in a room alone with a member of the opposite sex. If any of the above are violated, the punishment is castration!"

Netizens were baffled, not knowing what grudge existed between the two of them.

So, the ever-resourceful netizens quickly found Dongzi's snide remarks about Shi Yuzhu: "Some people create all sorts of fake health supplements and run tons of TV ads. After making tens of billions, now when people mention him, everyone thinks he's a godfather, a successful entrepreneur. As long as you have money, you're successful."

Well, what Dongzi said was quite on point.

After a simple breakfast, the group headed for the National Exhibition and Convention Center.

The format for this year's Sanguosha tournament had changed. After several discussions, it was decided that the top 16 teams would compete offline.

Six spots for the northern region, six for the southern region, and four for the Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan region.

Additionally, the eliminated quarter-finalist teams from each region were invited to watch the offline competition for free, with meals and accommodation covered, and train tickets reimbursed.

The top four from the Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan region were National Taiwan University, National Tsing Hua University (Taiwan), National Chengchi University, and the University of Hong Kong.

The other four quarter-finalists who were eliminated but invited to watch were: the University of Macau, National Chiao Tung University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and National Cheng Kung University.

Since the travel expenses from Taiwan to the mainland were too high and the procedures were rather troublesome, the players from National Chiao Tung and National Cheng Kung didn't make the trip, despite being invited to watch the finals.

The players from the University of Macau and the Chinese University of Hong Kong came. They treated it as a trip to the mainland, since Youke was arranging their food and lodging anyway.

Some even came early to attend the ChinaJoy expo.

"You guys are from Tsinghua too?"

"That's right, we've always been called Tsinghua. Our former president was also the president of Tsinghua when he was on the mainland."

"What a coincidence. We're brothers from the same mother."

The teams from the two Tsinghua Universities had already started chatting privately before the competition even began.

Some individuals among them didn't even know that there was another Tsinghua University across the strait.

Fortunately, no one started arguing about which one was more authentic on the spot.

In fact, public interaction between the two had started as early as 1993. In 1995, a graduate student exchange program was even launched.

But many students were still unaware of this.

"You can read simplified characters, right? Don't tell me you can't read the card descriptions later."

"We call them common-form characters, or cursive script. We use them often when writing letters and taking notes."

"Don't they use traditional characters over there?"

"Not traditional, they're standard-form characters."

During the Republican era, Chen Lifu had distributed a small booklet nationwide called *Standard Cursive Script Models*.

This booklet was once banned in Taiwan.

But in 1978, it was allowed to be published again and was reprinted several times.

Anyone who practiced cursive script according to that booklet would certainly be used to many simplified characters.

The simplified character for love (爱) is missing the heart (心)?

Over in Taiwan, the cursive form of the character for love also lacks a heart.

The cursive shorthand for "扰" is "扰". The cursive for "东" is "东". The cursive for "会" is "会". There are many such instances.

Not long after Chen Guiliang and the others sat down, leaders from the GAPP and relevant Shanghai departments began to arrive.

The leaders first shook hands with Chen Guiliang and his group, then with the university students. They were especially warm when meeting students from Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan, inquiring after their well-being and expressing that the mainland always welcomed them to come back for a visit.

Director Kou and other leaders sat in the front row and said to Chen Guiliang, "You've organized this event very well. It should be promoted more in the future. The Chinese people are one family, and this can be reflected in all aspects. Playing games together is also great. University students from both sides of the strait interacting through games to deepen their mutual understanding is a very natural process."

"Director Kou is right," said Chen Guiliang. "Just now, I saw the students from the two Tsinghua universities discussing their school histories. They were getting along very well."

Director Kou suggested, "After holding it in several major cities in the country, you could also try to hold the finals of the Sanguosha National Collegiate League across the strait."

Chen Guiliang said with a smile, "That would be a bit difficult. Sanguosha's Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan distributor would have to apply for and pass an approval process over there. As you know, relations have been very tense between the two sides these past two years."

"It'll probably be possible once Ah Bian steps down," Director Kou said.

"That's true." Chen Guiliang thought of the soon-to-be-inaugurated Ma-ge, and there really was hope of holding a competition in Taiwan.

In this era, an esports economy couldn't be established yet. Chen Guiliang was holding the Sanguosha league purely to expand its influence.

If it could really be broadcast on *Xinwen Lianbo*, the impact would be enormous.

Chen Guiliang wouldn't even need to promote it; the nation's print media would be scrambling to report on it.

Because it was so novel!

The official stance on online games was very contradictory. On one hand, they suppressed them, forbidding gaming programs from being broadcast on satellite channels. On the other hand, they vigorously supported domestic online games.

If *Sanguosha* appeared on *Xinwen Lianbo*, it would become the first online game to be acknowledged by CCTV.

Wouldn't the traditional media go crazy?

It would probably also spark a nationwide debate, with a war of words centered around "Should games be featured on *Xinwen Lianbo*?"

(End of this chapter)
